t: German rule began with Carl Peters' treaties with mainland chieftains and an imperial charter of 1885, and was imposed on the coast when Bismarck's warships forced the Sultan of Zanzibar to accept the German claims.
The conquest was marked by widespread atrocities, and the Maji Maji Rebellion of 1905 was crushed by measures to create a famine that may have cost as many as 300,000 lives.
After Germany's defeat in the First World War the colony was divided: Tanganyika went to Britain, Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium and the Kionga Triangle to Portugal.
dyk: Germany never formally abolished slavery in German East Africa: in 1914 officials considered a ban but did not make one, since they did not think it financially possible to compensate the owners.
ev: Bismarck signs an imperial charter granting Carl Peters' company a protectorate, and five German warships force the Sultan of Zanzibar to accept the German claims on the mainland
The Abushiri Revolt breaks out against the German East Africa Company and is put down with British help the following year
The Heligoland–Zanzibar Treaty fixes the border between German East Africa and the British East Africa Protectorate
The Hehe under Chief Mkwawa resist German expansion; after years of guerrilla war Mkwawa, cornered, kills himself in 1898
Governor Gustav Adolf von Götzen crushes the Maji Maji Rebellion by measures to create a famine, which may have cost as many as 300,000 lives
Chancellor Bernhard von Bülow appoints Bernhard Dernburg to reform the colonial administration after scandals of corruption and brutality
The Central Railroad reaches Lake Tanganyika, and Lettow-Vorbeck's forces defeat a British force more than eight times larger at the Battle of Tanga
The Paris Peace Conference awards the colony to Britain, which cedes Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium, while the Kionga Triangle goes to Portugal

f.founder: Carl Peters and his Society for German Colonization, under an imperial charter signed by Chancellor Otto von Bismarck in 1885
f.predecessor: The mainland claims of the Sultan of Zanzibar; the chiefdoms with which Peters signed treaties; the protectorate of the German East Africa Company
f.successor: Tanganyika (British), the districts of Ruanda and Urundi (Belgian) and the Kionga Triangle (Portuguese Mozambique), as League of Nations mandates from 10 January 1920
